fixed: **Library filters and search show the right files.** Clicking a smart view, changing a filter or typing a search quickly could show the previous list again when an older, slower reply arrived last; a reply from a superseded load is now ignored.
**The setup wizard stays closed when you close it.** On a slow connection a late "still open" save could land after "closed" or "done" and reopen the wizard; its saves now go out in order.

**Numbers are formatted for your region.** Counts on the Overview, in the Library tabs and smart views, Insights, History, System and the Workers dialog (such as 36609 files) now show with your region's thousands separator, 36,609 in English, 36.609 in German, 36 609 in French and 1,23,456 in Indian English, and decimals, percentages and sizes follow it too (1.5 GB, 1,5 GB). The region is the one of your language setting, or of your browser while the language is *Automatic*. This includes the sentences the server writes, such as the notification bell, task results and health checks, and the charts' text descriptions. Years, versions, ids, ports and file names are left as they are. The smoke tests now fail on any number without a separator, in English, German, French and the pseudo-locale.

**A fresh start could undo a just-finished change in the Library.** When PMM filled a new library index at start-up, a file whose analysis or commit finished at that moment could be shown with its older state (for example a converted file back as "to do"). The start-up fill now leaves any row that changed while it was reading.

**The top bar stays put on long pages.** Scrolling down a long page, such as Settings → Subtitles, slid the top bar up out of view after about one window height, and where the top bar wraps onto two rows (narrow windows, long languages) the Settings tabs slid under it. The top bar now stays at the top for the whole page, and the Settings tabs stick right below it, whatever its height.

**Safari no longer gets stuck on "PMM is offline".** One failed page load (the server restarting during an update, an iPad or iPhone waking up before its network is back) showed the offline page, and it only tried again when the browser reported going from offline to online, which it never did, so it stayed there while the server was up. The offline page now checks the server by itself every 10 seconds, when it is shown again and on **Try again**, and as soon as the server answers it removes the app's service worker and stored files and opens the app (the app installs them again). Opening a page now tries the server a second time before giving up, passes redirects (such as to the sign-in) on in the form Safari accepts, and leaves the sign-in pages (`/login`, `/setup`, `/auth/...`, a worker's `/sso`) and `/api/` to the browser. The app asks for the service worker without the browser's cache, so this fix reaches installed copies at the next visit.

new: **Pause and Resume a worker, or all of them, without faking it with pause hours.** A worker's own page has a **Pause / Resume** button (saved in its settings, so it survives a restart; the state reads "paused (by you)"), the Workers dialog has one per worker (admins, audit-logged as `worker_pause` / `worker_resume`), and a **Pause all workers** switch with an optional reason such as "NAS scrub" covers every worker and This server (audit-logged, shown on the Overview's live activity and in the Workers dialog). A pause lets the file in progress finish and takes no new work; either side's pause wins, and the reason says which. System → Health warns while all workers are paused. Older workers just obey the main app's pause. If you paused a worker with all-day pause hours, clear them. New `PUT /api/workers/{name}/settings` field `paused`, `GET`/`PUT /api/workers/pause-all`, the worker page's `PUT /api/pause`, and the worker setting `worker_paused` (use the button, not the form).

**The direct-play check covers many more devices and you choose which.** The item page now judges Fire TV (Stick HD / Lite, Stick 4K, 4K Max 1st and 2nd gen, Cube), Nvidia Shield, Fire TV on Vega OS, Chromecast with Google TV (HD and 4K), Chromecast casting, Google TV Streamer, Roku (4K / Ultra and HD), LG webOS, Samsung TVs by era, Xbox, PlayStation, iPhone / iPad, Android phones and tablets, and every Apple TV (HD, 4K 1st to 3rd gen and the 2026 4K 4th gen), each with its own codec, HDR, Dolby Vision, resolution, audio (including passthrough-only DTS / TrueHD) and subtitle limits. Pick the devices your household uses under Settings, Appearance, *Devices in the direct-play check* (`directplay_profiles`); the badge then reads like "Direct play on 6 of 7 devices". The default is a set of 17 common devices (every Apple TV, Plex Web, Roku, Fire TV, Android and Google TV, Samsung, iOS), to keep the item page short.

**The details suggest the one fix that helps several devices.** When two or more chosen devices (or Plex Web) only transcode because of audio (such as EAC3 or DTS) or because of image subtitles, the details say so, for example that a stereo AAC track would let Plex Web and 3 others direct play, or that a text copy of PGS subtitles (PMM can make one by OCR) would avoid burn-in. Nothing is planned or changed.

**Use the devices seen in Plex.** PMM now remembers the players Plex shows (model, platform, name, when last seen, files started) and a button beside the device choice ticks the matching profiles, listing the players it couldn't match (`GET /api/ops/direct-play/devices`). Model codes such as `AFTKRT` or `AppleTV14,1` are matched first, then keywords.
**Samsung and LG TVs burn in subtitles when the audio is transcoded**, which the check now predicts: a text subtitle shown together with EAC3 or DTS audio the TV can't play transcodes the video too.

**Scheduled tasks** and **System, Tasks** (`/system/tasks`, admins): every recurring job the main app runs (library sweep, Auto-apply, On Deck, Plex playback, artwork and labels, daily summary, update check, backups, the silent-worker check, trash purge, subtitle viewer cache clean-up, the Overview's live cards and the start-up fills) in one registry, with its schedule, last run, duration, result, next run, recent history and **Run now**. Tasks that are off say why and link to their setting; destructive ones (Trash purge, Auto-apply) ask first, and Auto-apply's Run now is refused while it is off and never applies more than a scheduled cycle would. Run now is audit-logged (`task_run_manual`); a failed run puts a notice in the bell. Ctrl+K lists the page. New `GET /api/ops/tasks`, `GET /api/ops/tasks/{id}/runs`, `POST /api/ops/tasks/{id}/run`.
**Update check** as a scheduled task (every 6 hours while *Check for updates* is on): the bell hears of a new version even when nobody opens the app. It shares the Updates page's cache.
**Subtitle viewer cache clean-up**, daily: expired texts are removed and the cache kept under its size (before, only reading and writing tidied it).

**Open a worker's page from the main app, signed in.** A worker's page can be reached from the network (its new setting *Reachable from the network*, applied at the next start, or `setup-worker.sh --remote-page`), and the Workers dialog then shows **Open page** for admins. The link goes through the main app, which hands the worker a 60-second, single-use sign-in token for that admin (signed with a key derived from the worker's key; audit-logged as *Worker page opened*); the worker's own password login keeps working. Keep the page on your own network (docs/workers.md, *Worker pages from the network*).

**Update now for out-of-date workers.** System → Updates shows, per worker, the newest compatible release in the workers' feed and an **Update now** button (admins, audit-logged): the worker finishes its current file, takes no new work, and its host updater installs the release at once, skipping the update hours and the self-update setting but never the compatibility, checksum or idle checks. The page follows the request live (requested, waiting for the current file, updating, done or failed with the reason). It needs the updater on that machine (`setup-worker.sh --self-update-timer`, which now also enables `pmm-worker-update.path`); older workers are updated by hand.

**Workers can update themselves from your NAS.** The new **Worker update feed** setting (Settings → Workers, advanced; default: the public feed) names the `releases.json` the workers' update timers read, e.g. the NAS's `https://pmm-builds.codershub.me/releases.json`; workers get it with their next check-in. `packaging/flatpak/write-lan-feed.py` writes that feed from the NAS's builds folder, checking each bundle against its `SHA256SUMS`.
changed: The Apple TV profile is now one per model; the old `apple_tv` id still works and means the Apple TV 4K (3rd gen); `samsung_tizen` means the 2020-2021 Samsung sets. The Roku profile now describes the 4K / Ultra models, and the direct-play texts say "devices" instead of "clients".

The two background loops (services and indexer) are replaced by one scheduler with the same timings: a 5-second tick, Plex every 30 seconds, On Deck every 15 minutes, artwork every 6 hours, the trash purge hourly, the sweep every `index_sweep_hours`, the daily summary and backups at their times; what ran at start-up still does. Each run is recorded in a new table, `task_runs` (the newest 50 per task), created at start-up; tasks not run at start-up pick up from their last run after a restart.
A failing trash purge, artwork listing or start-up fill is now recorded and reported in the bell (once until it works again) instead of being retried silently.
Long tasks run on their own threads, so a slow Plex call or backup no longer holds up the other background work.

`setup-worker.sh --remote-page` / `--no-remote-page` write or remove a systemd drop-in that opens the worker's page to the network (the unit itself is unchanged) and restart a running worker; it prints the firewall step for firewalld, ufw or SteamOS.

Worker protocol: optional `page` ({host, port, remote}) and `update_status` in the check-in, and `update_feed` and `update_now` in the heartbeat reply (`update_now` in progress replies too). Older workers and main apps ignore them; an older worker gets no Open page link and no Update now button.
The unused NAS-folder self-update engine (`pmm/safety/self_update.py`) is removed: workers update only through the update timer and the release feed.

new: **Hand back / Skip file** for a worker's current file (admins, audit-logged), in the Workers dialog and on the Overview's live cards. Hand back queues the file again for another worker; Skip file fails it ("skipped by <user>") and lists it on Problem files until retried. `POST /api/workers/{name}/task/hand-back` and `/task/skip`.

**Jobs per worker** (analysis, edits, conversions), set on the main app (Settings → Workers) and on the worker (`--jobs`, `--encoder none`); the stricter wins and existing workers keep every job. Meant for analysis-only CPU VMs with the media mounted read-only (docs/workers.md).
fixed: **Two workers no longer work on the same file.** Only the file's current worker may report progress or a result: a worker whose file was queued again, or that the main app forgot after a restart, is told to abandon it (stops its tools, deletes its scratch output, swaps nothing in), and a late result is ignored and logged. A file is queued again only after its worker has been silent about it for 10 minutes.

**Busy workers no longer show as offline.** Progress reports, results and hand-backs count as contact, and the current file is set as soon as a worker takes it, so the Workers dialog, the Overview cards, System → Health and Updates show it online with its file and percent. A worker renamed on its own page no longer leaves an offline entry under its old name.

**Worker progress no longer sticks at 0 %.** Every long analysis read (subtitle extraction, the sync-check speech, the full health check, audio decoding, voice detection, transcription) reports how far it is, on the main app and on the worker's own page.

**Reads that hang now fail instead of blocking a worker.** Every analysis read has a time limit scaled by the file's size, and `mkvmerge -J` and `ffprobe` have their own; the file fails with the step that hung and shows on System → Problem files. The speech read no longer deadlocks when FFmpeg prints many errors.

**The queue forecast now includes the analysis queue.** A new *Analysis queue finishes* line (Overview and Insights) shows the files waiting for analysis, the measured rate and "about N days, done around <date>", respecting the workers' quiet and pause hours. `GET /api/forecast` gains an `analysis` block.

**The Overview tells indexed and analysed files apart.** "Files analysed" is now "Files in the index" with a separate "Analysed" tile, and the Video codecs and Resolutions charts show never-analysed files as a "Not analysed yet" bar instead of an UNKNOWN codec or a "?" resolution.

**Insights no longer counts never-analysed files as fine.** Subtitle coverage has a grey "Not analysed yet" count and its shares, like the codec, language and HEVC-share figures, are of the analysed files. The panels have the normal 16 px spacing and the chart text keeps its normal size at any width (new token `--chart-text-size`).

**The What's new dialog is short again.** It shows the first sentence of each note (at most 6 per list, "All release notes" for the rest), scrolls inside itself and fits on a phone; `*emphasis*` and `_emphasis_` in release notes are rendered.

**System → Health no longer warns about the work queue while workers are busy.** It warns only when nothing is running, no worker is busy or has analysed lately, and This server is off. The Overview Activity says files and changes instead of "jobs queued".
changed: **Update the main app first; then update the workers too.** The main-app update alone already protects 0.6.0.0 workers from working on the same file twice (they are identified by their name header and already follow `cancel`). The workers need 0.6.0.1 for read progress, time limits and jobs per worker. No database change.

Worker protocol: optional `worker` (and `path`) in progress, done and release reports, `reason` with a `cancel` reply, `jobs` and `writes_media` in the check-in. Main apps and workers of either version keep working together (docs/workers.md, *Protocol additions*).

new: **Rich Discord messages**: finished applies, the daily digest and "Send test" are sent as embeds (summary, failed files first, size saved, tracks kept and removed, worker, poster thumbnail and a link to the item). New settings *Rich Discord messages* (on) and *PMM's public address* (empty: no links or posters). The other channels keep plain text, and Discord falls back to plain text if it refuses an embed.

**Plex labels** (off by default): one label per Plex item by its state (Cleaned, Needs review, Waiting; each name editable, empty turns one off). PMM only removes labels it recorded adding, renames move them, and Settings, Connections, Plex labels has *Preview changes* (dry run) and *Sync labels now* (admins, audit-logged). New table `plex_labels_applied`; new Plex client helper for edits (PUT).

**Queue forecast** on the Overview and Insights: when the queued work and the waiting changes will finish, per worker, and the projected space saved, from the workers' measured speeds, run window and quiet hours. New `GET /api/forecast` (cached 2 minutes). No media file is read.

**Learned encode presets** (setting *Learn quality settings*, off at first): verified conversions are recorded (table `conversion_history`); a worker about to search the HEVC quality is told the suggestion for a similar file (same series first). At confidence 0.8 or more with at least 3 results it skips the search (the full check of the encode still runs and a failure falls back to the normal search), otherwise the search covers a narrower range. The item page shows "Preset from <series> (confidence x)". Worker protocol: optional `preset` in a claimed task and `conversion` in the done report; older workers and main apps ignore them.

**Queue new imports from Sonarr and Radarr** (Settings, Connections, off by default): the webhook at `/api/arr/webhook` now understands On Import, On Upgrade, On Rename and On File Delete (and answers the Test button). An imported file is indexed at once and its analysis goes to the front of the worker queue (still a dry run; Auto-apply decides what is applied); a renamed file keeps its index row; a deleted file leaves the index; paths go through the Sonarr/Radarr path map; repeated events are ignored for 30 seconds; an import that needs review adds a bell notification. The webhook secret can be sent as `?token=` or an `X-PMM-Token` header. Settings: **Queue new imports** (`arr_queue_imports`, off) and **Ignore repeated events** (`arr_import_debounce_seconds`, 30). The Connections tab shows the address, the setup steps, the last call heard and a **Test** button (`GET /api/arr/imports`, `POST /api/arr/imports/test`, audit action `arr_import_test`).

**Subtitles viewer** on the item page (all four layouts): the file's subtitle tracks and sidecar subtitle files, a track's lines with timestamps in a virtualized list, search, and side-by-side compare of two tracks (full and forced, or a track against its clean-up). The text of an embedded track is read by a **worker** (the main app never reads the media file) and cached on the main app; sidecar files up to 2 MB are read directly; image subtitles say so. New `GET /api/library/items/{id}/subtitles` and `/subtitles/text`. Settings: **Subtitle viewer cache** (`subtitle_view_cache_mb`, 50) and **Keep viewed subtitles for** (`subtitle_view_cache_days`, 14).

**Title rules**: pin a title (*Never touch*) or override the library rules for one item, a season or a series: extra audio languages to keep, English commentary, full subtitles, a different subtitle profile, skip the HEVC conversion. Resolution order item > season > series > library rules. Pinned titles are skipped by the analysis passes and refused by Apply and Auto-apply (with the reason); a rule change re-plans the covered titles at once from their stored analysis. A badge on rows, cards and pages, a **Title rules** smart view, an editor on item, season and series pages, and **Settings, Libraries: Title rules** (admins change, everyone sees). Audit-logged, and carried by the settings export and import (`title_overrides`). New `GET/PUT /api/title-rules`, `GET /api/title-rules/for`, `DELETE /api/title-rules/{id}`, `POST /api/title-rules/preview`.

**Preview impact**: while a planning setting is unsaved, the Save bar says **This change affects N files**, by change type (audio removed or kept, subtitles removed or added, remux, conversion) and GB, with the list a page at a time. Worked out in a background task by re-planning every analysed file from its stored analysis: no media file is read. The title rule editor previews a rule the same way. New `POST /api/settings/preview-impact`, `GET`/`DELETE /api/settings/preview-impact/{id}`.

**Season check** on season and series pages: mixed codecs, resolutions, audio language sets, subtitle sets or missing forced subtitles, with per-episode details. The **Season inconsistent** smart view now also catches differing audio and subtitle sets. New `GET /api/library/season-check`.

**Watch-aware queue order** (Settings, Workers: Queue order, on by default): Plex's On Deck / Continue Watching first, then recently added files, then the rest; a running job is never pre-empted. On Deck comes from one cached Plex call every 15 minutes; without Plex, recently added goes first. The Overview and the item page show the reason.
changed: **Queue new imports** is new: **existing installs keep queueing imports** (it is switched on once at the first start of this version, unless it was saved before), and **new installs start with it off**. While it is off, webhook calls from Sonarr and Radarr are ignored.

Worker protocol: only additions. The subtitle viewer's request is an ordinary analysis task (placed first in the queue) with the existing `subtitles:<track id>` read, and the learned presets add an optional `preset` hint and `conversion` report, so workers of every version keep working (older ones just don't get or send those).
The database gets `title_rules`, `conversion_history` and `plex_labels_applied` tables and the library index a `title_rule` column, created at start-up. Back up before upgrading, as always.
The settings export's `title_overrides` now holds the title rules (it was an empty placeholder).

new: **Global search**: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac), or the search button in the top bar, finds films, series, seasons and episodes as you type, and also Settings and System pages and individual settings by name. Arrow keys, Enter and Esc work; recent searches are kept per user in the browser. New `GET /api/search`.

**Notification bell** in the top bar: what Discord and the other channels are told (finished applies, failed jobs, files that failed their check, films waiting for review, workers paused for heat, failed scheduled backups) is also kept in the app, with an unread count, links to the page concerned and read marks per account. Setting: Notifications to keep in the bell (200). New table `notifications` and `notification_reads`.
**Settings search**: a box on the Settings page finds a setting by label or help text across all tabs and jumps to it.
**Installable app (PWA)**: web manifest, icons and a service worker that keeps only the app shell, so PMM starts offline with a "PMM is offline" page. Nothing from `/api/` is ever cached.
**Bottom navigation bar** on phones (600 px and narrower) in place of the top tabs.

**Setup wizard** for a first run (Plex, Sonarr and Radarr, subtitles, libraries, workers, sign-in): opens for the first admin when nothing is configured, can be skipped, closed and continued, and run again from Settings, Account.

**Live activity** on the Overview: worker cards (current file, progress, fps, time left, GPU temperature and power, pause reason), the indexing rate and the queue size, pushed over server-sent events with reconnect and a polling fallback; shutdown is not held up by open streams.

**Smart views** on the Library: 4K not HEVC, Biggest savings, Missing forced subtitles, Made-up languages, Changed this week, Season inconsistent, and your own saved filters, each with a count and Apply all.
**Before and after** on the item page (all layouts) with space saved and estimated time; the Apply dialog totals the selection (files, GB before, after and saved, time on the online workers).
**Insights** page (`/insights`): codec mix, space reclaimed over time, subtitle coverage, audio language mix and a per-library breakdown, drawn as accessible inline SVG from a cached aggregate.

**Release notes** page (About, Release notes, `/releases`) with every version's New, Fixed and Changed lists, and a **What's new** dialog shown once per user after an upgrade (not on a fresh install). The changelog is shipped with the app.

**System, Updates** (admins): the installed version against the latest on the chosen channel (Release or Develop) with *Installed*, *Latest* and *Update available* badges, the release list from the public feed with highlights and notes links, the workers' versions against the main app (outdated and incompatible ones flagged), and how to update. A dot on the About button shows an available update. The main app only looks the feed up (5 second timeout, cached 6 hours, a soft warning when it fails) and never updates itself. Settings, System, Updates: **Check for updates** and **Update channel**.

**Export and import settings** (Settings, System, admins): one JSON file with all settings, the libraries, layouts and each user's own appearance. Secrets are left out unless chosen (and then the file is marked). An import is validated, shown as a preview grouped by Settings tab (secrets only as "will be set/changed") and applied on confirmation; unknown keys are reported, not applied; it is audit-logged.
fixed: The top bar wraps onto a second row instead of pushing the page sideways when the window is narrower or the language longer.
changed: The database gets two new tables (`notifications`, `notification_reads`), created at start-up.

The library index gets three columns (`conlang`, `audio_langs`, `sub_langs`) and a partial index, filled once in the background from stored plans at the first start. Back up before upgrading, as always.

new: A **System** section for admins (Health, Problem files, Logs, Audit, Backup) at `/system/<page>`; see docs/operations.md.

**Health**: status cards (OK, warning, fail) with a fix hint for the database, disk space, Plex, Sonarr, Radarr and Bazarr, workers, queue, tools and recent errors, also as JSON (`GET /api/ops/health`).
**Problem files**: files that keep failing or can't be read, with Retry and Ignore; the item page warns about them.

**Direct-play advisor** on the item page (all four layouts): whether Plex Web, Apple TV, Roku, Android TV, smart TVs and the desktop app would direct play, direct stream or transcode the file, and why, from the index alone.

**Backups**: back up now, scheduled (daily or weekly, keep the newest N), download, delete, and restore from a file with a preview and a confirmation; the file is validated first and the current database is kept as a backup. Secrets are left out unless you ask, and marked when included.
**Audit log** of sign-ins, account and role changes, settings changes, applies, restores, backups and trash deletions, with filters.

**Logs** viewer: the app now writes a rotating log file; live tail, level, text and file filters, download and clear. Tokens, API keys, passwords, cookies and Authorization headers are redacted in what you see and download.
**Metrics**: `/metrics` (Prometheus) and `/metrics.json` (Home Assistant), off by default, protected by a token or a private-network check.
Settings, System tab: backups, metrics and the log file.

Every rewritten file is verified before it replaces the original: its streams, languages, flags and codecs are compared with the plan, its duration with the source's, a few seconds are decoded (start, middle and end with Full) and every subtitle track is read. A file that fails keeps the original untouched and the item fails with the reason. On by default (Settings, Safety and housekeeping: Full, Quick or Off, which asks for a confirmation); workers check their rewrites the same way.

Worker limits (Settings, Workers, and per worker with its Limits button): no new job while a worker's GPU is too hot (83 °C by default, until it is 10 °C cooler) or draws too much power, and none in its quiet hours (e.g. Mon-Fri 22:00-07:00). A running file always finishes, unless the GPU reaches the hard limit (92 °C): then it is handed back untouched and queued again. GPU readings are read-only (nvidia-smi, or the driver's NVML inside the Flatpak). The Workers dialog and the Overview show why a worker waits, and the Workers dialog shows each GPU's temperature.

Workers can update themselves (opt-in per worker): a systemd user timer on the worker machine (`setup-worker.sh --self-update-timer`) installs a newer release from the public feed when it works with the main app, inside the worker's update hours, and only while the worker is idle. The worker's Flatpak gets no host permission. Updates start once worker bundles are published in the feed (not yet in this release). See docs/workers.md.
changed: The database gets two new tables, `audit_log` and `problem_ignores`, created automatically at start-up. Back up before upgrading, as always.

new: The web UI can be translated (phase 1): each user picks a language in Settings, Account; English is complete and other languages can be added as JSON files (see docs/ui.md). Server-side texts and the command line stay English for now.

Themes: System, Light or Dark per user, plus custom themes (presets Plex orange, High contrast and OLED black, live preview with contrast checks, import/export as JSON), with no flash of the wrong theme; light and dark colours now meet WCAG AA contrast.
fixed: Subtitles held for your burned-in review no longer count as a failed search: once you decide, the next run adds them instead of waiting a day.
Text that was hard to read in the light theme (accent text, warnings, the Commit button) now has enough contrast.
The Settings tabs wrap onto a second line instead of being cut off, and Settings panels fit narrow phones, in any language.
changed: The code is reorganised into smaller modules, with no change in behaviour.

Every pull request and develop build now runs the full test suite with the real media tools, plus browser tests of every page in light and dark at desktop and phone size; a failing run blocks the Docker image.
Browsers check for updated scripts and styles on every load, so an upgrade never shows a stale page.

new: Subtitle clean-up driven by Bazarr, with rules for PGS (picture) subtitles.
Fallback for films that never get forced subtitles.
Two ways to manage subtitles: Bazarr, or PMM's own built-in search and download with scoring, timing checks, retries, upgrades and quota handling.
Films without dialogue are recognised and don't need subtitles.
Optional subtitle position strip: SRT subtitles can be kept at the bottom of the screen (styled ASS subtitles keep their placement and effects).
Sign in with Authentik (OpenID Connect), including automatic sign-in.
Library views with switchable layouts (list, grid, item page styles) and artwork from Plex.
Libraries: choose the folders to index (or import them from Plex); everything is analysed continuously as a dry run on your workers, with nothing changed until you apply.
A new Overview home page with activity and workers, per-library tabs, readable page addresses and breadcrumbs.
"This server" setting: the main app can help process files, off by default so a NAS stays light.
Auto-apply: opt-in automatic applying of chosen change types (off by default).
MP4 and AVI files are planned for conversion to MKV (a remux, no re-encode) instead of being skipped.
Plex-aware pausing: a worker pauses only when Plex is busy on its machine or playing the file it's working on, and a rewritten file is never swapped in during playback.
Release feed and version scheme: four-part versions, with Develop and Release channels.
fixed: Foreign films keep their original-language audio instead of the dub.
Made-up languages (such as Klingon or Elvish) never lead to "English only, remove all subtitles".
Discord notifications work again.
Workers stop gracefully: the running file is handed back and cleaned up, and the worker service starts and logs correctly.
Free space is shown correctly for a scratch folder that doesn't exist yet.
changed: The Settings page has been redesigned.
The Review page is retired; its work now lives in the library tabs.
The Docker image is published under version tags (`0.2.0.0`, `0.2`, `latest`); preview builds are tagged `develop`.
PMM is licensed under the GPL-3.0-or-later.

new: **Sign in automatically** with OpenID Connect: a signed-out visitor goes straight to the provider (Authentik) and back to the page they asked for, and the password form sits behind a "Use password instead" link. The new setting `oidc_auto_login` is on by default, and API calls still get a 401.
**Library artwork from Plex.** Posters, backdrops, stills and series posters are fetched through Plex (the token stays on the server) and cached on disk with a size cap (`plex_art_cache_mb`).

**Switchable Library layouts.** The item page can be Classic, Cinematic, Sidebar or Glass and the list can be rows or a poster grid; each user's choice is saved, and Settings, Appearance sets everyone's default. A new layout is one file plus one registry line.
**Previous and next episode** links on the item page, and a made-up-language signal in the item details.
fixed: **Foreign films keep the original-language audio, not the dub.** The original language comes from Radarr or Sonarr, then TMDB, then the track flagged as original, then the only non-English language; with several and no way to tell, all are kept and the plan says so.

**Styled ASS subtitles keep their placement and effects.** The position, colour and italic strip switches no longer touch ASS/SSA tracks, and their clean-up only drops blank untagged events, plain ads and exact duplicates.
**Signing in from the plain login page lands on the home page**, not back on the login page.
**The Library item page has even spacing** between panels and equal-height rows, and the Library navigation is readable over backdrops.

new: **Library index and Library pages.** Every file has one row with a state for video, audio and subtitles, an overall status and a one-line summary, kept current after dry runs, commits and restores. The Library has a file list with To do, Waiting, Needs review, Done, Failed and All tabs, Movies / TV / All, search, sort and multi-select with *Apply selected* (admins), TV by series and season, and a deep-linkable page per file with tracks, review notes, history with restore, *Re-analyse* and *Apply this*.

**PMM's own subtitle downloads** (Path B) work without Bazarr. Candidates from OpenSubtitles are scored (hash, ids, release, frame rate, hearing-impaired, trust, downloads), tried best first until one passes the timing check, retried with backoff, upgraded later, and kept within the daily download quota.
**Films without dialogue** (all main audio tracks marked zxx) want no subtitles and count as complete on both subtitle paths.
**Commits can take planned files from several dry runs** in one job.
fixed: **Discord notifications work again.** Notifications now send an app user agent (Discord answered 403 to Python's default one), and the test button shows the reason when it fails.
**Downloaded full subtitles get the same default flag** as an embedded track would, and an upgrade keeps the flags of the track it replaces.
**PMM's own pending downloads show when they will next be tried**: the library waits until the next search or the quota reset instead of showing a placeholder.

new: **Two ways to manage subtitles.** Bazarr (as before) or PMM's own wanted-subtitles profile (`subtitle_profile_default`, `_anime`, `_foreign`), chosen with `subtitle_source` (auto, bazarr or local). Reports say which source decided; `pmm scan --compare-sources` plans each file both ways and shows where they differ, and an *Import from Bazarr* button fills the profile from Bazarr's language profiles.

**Subtitle formatting strip.** SRT subtitles can be kept at the bottom of the screen, with optional removal of colours and italics, bold and underline; a track that only needs this is planned as a remux, and held Bazarr items are left alone.
**Worker GPU test** now reports the SSIM quality and size saving on a clip that HEVC can actually shrink.
fixed: **The worker GPU test encodes its clip loosely** so that HEVC really runs (tested on a GTX 1080 Ti).

new: **Bazarr-driven clean-up.** PMM asks Bazarr whether an item's subtitles are complete before touching it, removes unwanted subtitle files next to the video, and handles audio with its own settings. An item counts as complete when only forced English is missing and an embedded forced PGS exists.
**Picture (PGS) forced subtitles become text.** A forced PGS track is replaced by a validated SRT or OCR text track after a timing match against the existing subtitles.

**Films that will never get forced subtitles.** When Bazarr lists only English forced as missing forever, PMM waits (`forced_missing_wait_days`, default 30) and then decides locally: it makes forced subtitles from the full ones, or removes all subtitles when there is no foreign dialogue, or holds the file for review.

**Made-up languages are never treated as English-only.** Language tags such as "[speaking Klingon]", non-English text, non-natural language codes and a list of known titles (`conlang_titles`) keep subtitles in place, and a forced track is built from the tagged lines.

**Sign in with Authentik (OpenID Connect).** Accounts have admin and view-only roles from the provider's admin group, local password sign-in can be turned off once an admin has signed in through OIDC, and `PMM_FORCE_LOCAL_LOGIN=1` brings it back.
**Workers stop gracefully.** On a stop the worker cancels its running tool, deletes its scratch files and hands the file back to the main app at once.
**`pmm scan --apply` notifies Plex, Sonarr, Radarr and Bazarr** after a change, as the web UI does.
fixed: **Held items never get subtitle properties edited**, and the plan report shows which properties an edit would change.
**A forced track with too few lines** is reported as "not measured" instead of "left unchanged for review".

**The worker service stops cleanly.** `systemctl stop` no longer leaves the old worker holding its port, its log lines are tagged `pmm-worker` and written whole, and About shows the worker's real scratch folder, including the free space of one that does not exist yet.
changed: **The Settings page is redesigned** with tabs per group in task order, units and percentages, an Advanced part, conditional settings, a "set / not set" badge, connection checks with a test button, unsaved-change dots and a phone layout. Sonarr and Radarr have their own sections.
**Subtitle downloads by PMM pause while Bazarr is set up**, and the Settings page says so.

new: **Workers can be set up on Fedora, Bazzite and RHEL.** `setup-worker.sh` checks the machine, installs the NVIDIA extension matching the driver and prints the steps for the distribution; a loaded driver without its extension is reported in the worker page, its log and the main app.
**Always-on switch on the worker page** ("Start this worker when I log in"), through the desktop's background portal in the Flatpak.

**About pages** on the main app and the worker with the version, exact build, how it is installed, the machine (system, CPU, memory, GPU, driver), uptime, data folder, database size and scratch space.

**Foreign dialogue is never missed, made-up languages included.** Forced subtitles can be made from the film's own full subtitles (each line's audio gets a language check, and picture subtitles are read with OCR), Whisper flags speech in no known language instead of translating it into nonsense, and an English film never loses its only English subtitles when no forced ones can be had.
fixed: **Workers in the media's group can use the trash.** The trash folder copies its parent's group write, and SMB access errors now say that the NAS decides for the credentials' user.
**Thor: The Dark World no longer loses its only subtitle track.** TMDB lists only English for it, so no forced subtitles were sought; OpenSubtitles is now searched whatever TMDB says.

new: **Accounts and login.** The first visit creates the account (scrypt-hashed password), then a login page with 30-day sessions; failed logins are limited and `pmm reset-password` fixes a lockout.

**Settings in the database.** 67 settings with types and limits are saved in the database, applied without a restart, with secrets write-only; the Settings tab also holds worker keys and the Plex webhook address.
**A key per worker**, created in the UI, stored hashed, revocable, with its last use shown. Compose files no longer carry a password or shared token.

**Worker settings and status page.** Each worker serves its own page (127.0.0.1:8766) with its connection, current file and progress, pauses, GPU, encoders and recent files, and keeps its settings (main app address, key, name, path map, encoder, scratch folder, pause rules, Whisper model) in its own database.

**Burned-in subtitle check.** Before a subtitle line is added, the frames behind it are read with Tesseract OCR; lines already burned into the picture are left out and unclear films are held for review in the Library (Yes / No, undoable, `pmm burned-in`).
**Existing forced subtitles are recognised** next to the video (for example `Thor (2011).en.forced.srt`), and TMDB's spoken languages stop Whisper from listening to films that are English only.
**The Docker image is published to GHCR** (`ghcr.io/codyrwhite/plexmediamanager`, for amd64 and arm64) and the compose files pull it.
fixed: **Write access is checked before any work on a file.** A worker that cannot write to the NAS no longer runs Whisper first and then fails moving the original to the trash; the error names both user ids.
**Forced subtitles are timed more precisely** against the film's full English subtitles, then the speech, then the foreign speech.
**Build folders are kept out of the Flatpak and Docker builds**, which stopped a 2.5 GB folder from stalling the build.
**The top bar wraps on phones** instead of scrolling sideways.

new: **Workers that share a machine with Plex can pause.** Each worker can have pause hours (`--pause-hours 16:00-23:30`) and pause while Plex has N transcodes; a paused worker takes no new files and its running encode is frozen and resumed later.

**GPU-first routing of conversions.** Unoptimised conversions go to GPU workers, CPU (x265) workers take only what no GPU worker can do, and a GPU worker hands a file back untouched when NVENC cannot make it smaller and visually lossless.
**The Docker image runs with PUID, PGID, UMASK and TZ variables**, like the Sonarr and Radarr images, so files it rewrites keep their owner.

**Synology install guide and tested compose file** with step-by-step DSM 7.2 Container Manager instructions, and an option to give the container its own IP on an existing macvlan network with media at Plex's paths.
fixed: **Whisper picks the precision each GPU supports** (8-bit on a GTX 1080 Ti, 16-bit on RTX 20-series and newer) instead of refusing to load.
**NVENC uses only the optional settings each GPU accepts**, so a card that rejects one option no longer falls back to slow x265.
**NVENC settings remember the GPU they were tested on**, and a machine with a different GPU searches again on its own card.
**A paused worker no longer loses its job.** Workers check in every 15 seconds while a task runs, so a frozen encode is not marked failed after 10 minutes.
**GPU names show inside the Flatpak**, files without size tags (MKVs muxed by FFmpeg) are converted, and preview clips work without libx264.

new: **MKV audio and subtitle clean-up.** Non-anime files keep the best English audio and English forced subtitles; anime keeps the English dub first, then the native audio, with forced and full English subtitles. Changes are made in place with mkvpropedit where possible and with a verified remux otherwise.

**Forced-subtitle sync with a confidence check.** PMM's own aligner (voice detection and cross-correlation) measures timing against the full English track, refuses low-confidence corrections and detects frame-rate drift. Picture (PGS) subtitles can serve as the reference.

**Web UI** with a dry run you review before committing: folder browser, per-file track review, selective commit, live progress, cancel, an activity log and a hardware panel. A commit refuses files changed since the dry run.

**Quality-checked HEVC conversion** (x265, NVENC, VideoToolbox) that only keeps a result that is smaller and stays visually lossless (VMAF and SSIM floor), plus MP4, AVI and TS to MKV without re-encoding. Files that are not HEVC or not MKV are flagged.

**Settings optimiser** that tests quality settings on samples across the film, picks one for best quality, balanced or most savings, and shows matching frames, difference images and a real HEVC preview clip.
**Remote workers** run conversions on other machines through the network share (`pmm worker`), with a token-protected worker API and a Workers panel.

**Library dashboard, History with restore and a trash.** Results are stored and paged, interrupted runs resume, originals go to a drive-level trash with one-click restore, and the Library shows charts and what needs attention.

**Plex, Sonarr, Radarr and notifications.** PMM pauses work while someone is watching in Plex, refreshes the changed folder, rescans in Sonarr and Radarr, supports an automatic mode for new files, and notifies through Discord, ntfy, Pushover or a webhook.
**Subtitle clean-up** removes ads and watermarks, repairs mis-decoded text, drops empty lines and merges repeats, with an optional hearing-impaired tag removal.
**Missing subtitles can be found or generated** with OpenSubtitles and Whisper (faster-whisper) on workers that support it.
**Flatpak and Docker packages** for SteamOS and a Synology NAS, with a Whisper extension for GPU machines.
